## The project

This project turns a master's thesis on parametric insurance into open outputs: the Python library [`parametric_insurance_design`](https://github.com/marc272/parametric-insurance-design), this site with its explorers and posts, and a paper. They present the thesis's two ideas, the [tail-risk objective](method/tail-risk-objective.qmd) and [portfolio (joint) calibration](method/portfolio-calibration.qmd), each on its own and [in combination](method/combination.qmd).

## The thesis

*Tail-Risk-Optimized Payout Design in Parametric Insurance*, a master's thesis by Marc Prinzing at the Technical University of Munich. The thesis isn't public. Its code is, at [marc272/parametric-insurance-framework](https://github.com/marc272/parametric-insurance-framework), and the library is checked against it.

## How to read the numbers

The site never runs an optimisation. It reads results that the library computed and exported, and every number it shows comes with its setup: the portfolio, the basis (what an outcome is), the basis-risk model, the pricing, and the split between calibration and test years. Placeholder pages are labelled as such.

The site describes the method and the tool. It makes no general claim that either idea, or their combination, outperforms the alternatives.
